newsitem.title: BURMA: Suu Kyi slams Burma for growing repression.
newsitem.headline: Suu Kyi slams Burma for growing repression.

text.p: Burmese democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi on Tuesday lashed out at the military government for what she termed continued repression of the opposition and vowed to continue her fight for democracy.

"This is persecution of the NLD," Suu Kyi told a news conference after outlining arrests and intimidation tactics taken by the government against members of her National League for Democracy (NLD) party. "The situation is getting worse all the time."
Suu Kyi, who won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize for her democracy drive, said her movements were still restricted by the government but defined herself and her party as "fighting fit".
She said the government's continued efforts to intimidate the NLD into resigning from the party showed it wanted to give the impression the NLD was lacking support.

"I think what they are trying to do is to stop the people from supporting the NLD," she told a news conference held at a house outside the barricades blocking access to her street. "It is supposed to appear as though public support for the NLD has waned."
The NLD won 1990 general elections by a landslide but was never allowed to assume power. Suu Kyi, daughter of independence leader Aung San, was released from six years of house arrest in July 1995.
